note:
**The 1881 round, schedules 185 to 211 - Tunnel Road, Lincoln Circus, Duke William Mount, Newcastle Circus, North Road, Tattershall Drive, Pelham Terrace and Newcastle Drive.** Transcribed by A. Hagues as the images came in.

## The Newcastle Drive Rule, confirmed a third time and sharpened

**The record's rule is that a Newcastle Drive number equals 39 minus the old Pelham Terrace number**, the renumbering dated to 1894-5 by the Bromley account. These pages confirm it again and change what it means.

**The enumerator calls the street Newcastle Drive and numbers it as Pelham Terrace, in the same book.** Schedule 201 is "4 Pelham Terrace" and schedule 202 is "6 and 8 Pelham Terrace", but schedules 203 and 204 are "10 Newcastle Drive" and "14 Newcastle Drive" - even numbers the record's Newcastle Drive does not have, because it runs 1 to 39 odd.

**Schedule 204 settles it beyond argument.** It is **John Jardine, 56, lace machine maker employing 162 hands**, at "14 Newcastle Drive". The record already holds him in 1891 at **"14 Pelham Terrace (now 25 Newcastle Drive)"**, aged 66 - ten years exactly. And 39 minus 14 is 25.

**So the name changed before the numbers did.** By 1881 the street was already being called Newcastle Drive by some hands and Pelham Terrace by others, while the numbering stayed on the old sequence for another fourteen years. See [[newcastle-drive-rule-name-before-number]].

Three households are filed by the rule, and in every case the source line keeps the figure the page actually wrote, so the reading can be undone: **schedule 201 to 35 Newcastle Drive** (page: 4 Pelham Terrace), **203 to 29** (page: 10 Newcastle Drive), **204 to 25** (page: 14 Newcastle Drive). Schedules 208, 210 and 211 give 5, 3 and 1, which are odd and therefore already on the new sequence, and are filed as written.

**Schedule 202 cannot be filed, because it is two houses.** Elise Courtial's **Bruncliffe** occupies **6 and 8 Pelham Terrace** - 33 and 31 Newcastle Drive by the rule - and a household cannot be filed to two properties. It is the largest household in the round: a French principal, teachers of music, German, drawing and English from Germany, Ireland, Bath and Colchester, and **thirty-one pupils, including girls born in Calcutta, Ceylon and Victoria**.

## Other things these pages say

**1871 schedule 132 is now placed.** Sigismund Hamel, a Hamburg lace merchant the 1871 book puts on "Newcastle Terrace", is at **3 Newcastle Drive** here with four of his daughters, every age +10. The 1871 household is filed accordingly.

**10 Park Drive is not in the property list.** Richard Dexter's household - a cigar manufacturer employing 200 girls, with nine sons in the house - is left unfiled. Park Drive runs 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 9 in the record.

**Two households are given the same address.** Schedules 195 and 196 both read 3 North Road. Both are left unfiled rather than one of them guessed at.

**Houses the record does not hold by name**: Cavendish Villas on Duke William Mount (twice), Durham Lodge on Newcastle Circus, Claremont on North Road.

**A household that reaches the Falkland Islands.** At 1 Newcastle Drive the Baillons - French, in Nottingham since at least 1871 - have a son farming sheep in the Falklands and two grandchildren born there, with four Irish servants in the house. Whether this is the same family the 1871 book calls **Alexis C A Baillon** on Newcastle Terrace is not settled: the ages drift five and six years and three forenames disagree, so no placement is made.

**Readings that could go either way are flagged in the source line.** Infants are entered as age 0 with the real age kept in the source. Repeated names carry a birth year and are matched on it.
source: 1881 census enumerator's book, Standard Hill and Limits of the Castle of Nottingham, schedules 185 to 211, transcribed by A. Hagues.
